facts.text: This was shot as Love Crimes, but producers learned a bigger-budget film starring Sean Young was being made at the same time. They renamed it Carnal Crimes.
VideoHound's Golden Movie Retriever sums up Carnal Crimes as "well-acted upscale softcore trash." It also notes an unrated version of the film was sold on video.
Director Alexander Hippolyte is really Gregory Dark, half of the adult-film team the Dark Brothers. He also worked as Gregory Hippolyte and Gregory Brown.
The rival Love Crimes, directed by Lizzie Borden, hit theaters in January 1992 via Miramax. It earned about $2.3 million on a $6 million budget, and star Sean Young got a Razzie nomination.
Gregory Dark trained as a fine artist with an MFA from Stanford, then studied film at NYU, before making hardcore films and later erotic thrillers like this one.
Gregory Dark ran production at B-movie outfit Axis Films, directing or producing 30+ action films and erotic thrillers from 1987 to 1995. Sight & Sound called his thrillers groundbreaking.
Paula Trickey (Jasmine) was crowned Miss Oklahoma in the 1985 All-American Teen Pageant, a Miss USA production. She lost the finals to an unknown named Halle Berry.
Julie Strain (Ingrid) became Penthouse Pet of the Month in June 1991, the year of this film. She later married Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles co-creator Kevin Eastman.
Paula Trickey (Jasmine) later got her biggest role as Sgt. Cory McNamara on the USA Network bike-cop series Pacific Blue, which ran from 1996 to 2000.
Danny Trejo plays a ticket agent here, years before Machete. He got into acting after a 1985 set visit on Runaway Train as a drug counselor, which led to a job as an extra.
Doug Jones (Lang) was the moon-faced McDonald's crooner Mac Tonight in 27 of 29 commercials. In 1989 Bobby Darin's son sued over the Mack the Knife parody and the ads largely stopped.
Julie Strain was the voice and model for the lead in Heavy Metal 2000. Her work spanned 100+ films, earning her the nickname Queen of the B-movies.
Doug Jones (Lang) went on to play the Faun and the Pale Man in Pan's Labyrinth and Saru in 58 episodes of Star Trek: Discovery. This direct-to-video thriller was an early credit.
Martin Hewitt (Renny) beat out 5,000 actors, reportedly including Tom Cruise and Timothy Hutton, to star in Endless Love (1981). He'd been a bartender and valet parker.
Martin Hewitt (Renny) was nominated for a Razzie for Worst New Star for his debut Endless Love (1981). The film still grossed about $32 million on a $9.7 million budget.
Martin Hewitt (Renny) later left acting. He now lives in Morro Bay, California, where he runs a home inspection business and does local theater.
Andre Rosey Brown, who plays a detective here, was a real cop. He spent about 14 years with the Inglewood Police Department while acting, and he was Cash's cellmate in Tango & Cash.
Yvette Nelson (Mia), credited as Yvette Stefens, was a Frederick's of Hollywood model on a 7-year contract and had a Maybelline campaign at 23.
Andre Rosey Brown played football at Rocky Mountain College and worked as a jazz drummer before policing and acting. He later played the umpire in Space Jam and died in 2006 at age 50.
Gregory Dark later directed music videos including Linkin Park's One Step Closer, Britney Spears' From the Bottom of My Broken Heart and Xzibit's What U See Is What U Get.
Danny Trejo, the ticket agent here, was a San Quentin boxing champ. In Heat (1995) his character was named Trejo for his uncle, and he improvised his death scene with Robert De Niro.
Gregory Dark made the 2006 slasher See No Evil, starring wrestler Kane. It grossed almost $19 million worldwide on an $8 million budget, plus over $45 million in DVD sales and rentals.
Julie Strain (Ingrid) suffered head trauma in a fall from a horse that caused retrograde amnesia. In January 2020 a studio wrongly reported her death. She died on January 10, 2021, aged 58.
This was Gregory Dark's first erotic thriller. He still made adult films that year, including New Wave Hookers 2, per Bands About Movies' Gregory Dark Week review.
Danny Trejo's Machete began as a side character in Spy Kids (2001), then led to Machete (2010) and Machete Kills (2013). He now owns Trejo's Tacos and other Los Angeles restaurants.
Doug Jones, cast as Lang, later became famous playing creatures under heavy makeup. Here he appears without any makeup, as Bands About Movies noted.
